title: Web Accessibility Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Web Accessibility course.

entries.name: Use a real button
entries.summary: A button already knows how to work with a keyboard.

entries.name: Give the page a clear outline
entries.summary: Headings tell readers how a page is organised.

example.code:
Our school garden

Plants

We grow beans.

Jobs

Watering

Water in the morning.

entries.name: Name important page regions
entries.summary: Elements such as nav and main name big page regions.

example.code:
Garden club

Plants

Plants

Beans grow here.

entries.name: Write useful image words
entries.summary: Alternative text describes a useful image for someone who cannot see it.

entries.name: Label a form field
entries.summary: A visible label explains what to type. Matching its for value with an input id links the two parts.

entries.name: Connect help text
entries.summary: A field can have a short help message as well as a label.

example.code: Use the name shown on your club card.

entries.name: Keep keyboard focus clear
entries.summary: Focus is the place that will receive the next key action.

entries.name: Add a skip link
entries.summary: A skip link lets a keyboard user move past repeated navigation and straight to the main content.

example.code:
Skip to main content
Home

Today's reading

Pick a short story.

entries.name: Make links explain their destination
entries.summary: Link words should make sense when read on their own.

example.code:
Read the garden club timetable

Garden club timetable

We meet on Friday.

entries.name: Explain a result in words
entries.summary: A polite live region can announce a small update without moving keyboard focus.

entries.name: Respect less-motion settings
entries.summary: Some people feel unwell when a page moves a lot.

example.code: Reading card

entries.name: Check a page in several ways
entries.summary: Accessibility testing needs more than one check.

example.code:
1. Use Tab and Shift+Tab through the page.
2. Activate controls with Enter or Space.
3. Zoom text and page to 200%.
4. Check labels and error messages.
5. Run an automated accessibility check.
6. Try the main task with a screen reader.
